texts: Welcome to Quiz Rush! Today's challenge is tough. Forty famous football stadiums are hiding behind a puzzle. The pieces flip one by one, but never all of them. You have ten seconds each. Ready? Let's play!
Kick-off! The first stadium is hiding behind the puzzle. Which one is it?
Yes! It's Wembley Stadium, in London. England's national stadium reopened in 2007 after a full rebuild.
Piece by piece... which legendary ground is this?
That's Camp Nou, in Barcelona. FC Barcelona has played here since 1957.
Watch the tiles flip! Can you name this stadium?
It's Santiago Bernabeu, in Madrid. Real Madrid's home since 1947.
Big clue: you've seen this one on TV a thousand times. Which stadium?
Correct answer: Old Trafford, in Manchester. Manchester United's home is nicknamed the Theatre of Dreams.
This one has seen two World Cup finals. Name it!
Of course, it's Maracana, in Rio de Janeiro. It hosted the World Cup final in both 1950 and 2014.
Two clubs, one home. Which stadium is under there?
Boom! It's San Siro, in Milan. AC Milan and Inter share this famous ground.
Look at that shape! Which stadium is this?
Here it is: Allianz Arena, in Munich. Its outer shell can light up in different colours.
You'll never walk alone with this one. Which ground is it?
You got it, it's Anfield, in Liverpool. Liverpool FC has played here since 1892.
A national stadium is hiding here. Which one?
Spot on! It's Stade de France, in Saint-Denis. It hosted the 1998 World Cup final.
Last easy one! Listen for the roar. Which stadium is this?
The answer is Westfalenstadion, in Dortmund. Its famous south stand is known as the Yellow Wall.
Medium round! South American fans, this one's for you. Which stadium is hiding now?
Yes! It's La Bombonera, in Buenos Aires. The home of Boca Juniors.
Altitude and history. Which stadium is under the tiles?
That's Estadio Azteca, in Mexico City. It hosted the World Cup final in 1970 and 1986.
Paris lights are on. Which ground is this?
It's Parc des Princes, in Paris. The home of Paris Saint-Germain.
Scotland calling! Which stadium is it?
Correct answer: Celtic Park, in Glasgow. The home of Celtic Football Club.
Champions League nights live here. Name this stadium!
Of course, it's Estadio da Luz, in Lisbon. Benfica's home hosted the Champions League final in 2014 and 2020.
A legend gave this stadium his name. Which one is it?
Boom! It's Johan Cruyff Arena, in Amsterdam. Ajax's home was renamed after Johan Cruyff in 2018.
Olympic history in this one. Which stadium is it?
Here it is: Olympiastadion Berlin, in Berlin. Built for the 1936 Olympics, it hosted the 2006 World Cup final.
Two rival clubs share this one too. Which stadium is it?
You got it, it's Stadio Olimpico, in Rome. AS Roma and Lazio share this stadium.
One of Spain's oldest grounds. Which one?
Spot on! It's Mestalla, in Valencia. Valencia CF has played here since 1923.
Last Medium question! A stadium right in the city centre. Name it!
The answer is St James' Park, in Newcastle. Newcastle United's ground sits right in the city centre.
Hard round! Fewer tiles, more pressure. Which stadium is this?
Yes! It's Estadio do Dragao, in Porto. FC Porto's home opened in 2003.
A Dutch classic is hiding here. Which one?
That's De Kuip, in Rotterdam. Feyenoord has played here since 1937.
Back to Glasgow, but which stadium this time?
It's Ibrox, in Glasgow. The home of Rangers Football Club.
London calling! Which ground is under the puzzle?
Correct answer: Stamford Bridge, in London. Chelsea has played here since the club was founded in 1905.
This one is brand new and full of tech. Which stadium?
Of course, it's Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, in London. Opened in 2019, it has a retractable pitch for NFL games.
A cathedral of football in Spain. Can you name it?
Boom! It's San Mames, in Bilbao. Athletic Club's new San Mames opened in 2013.
Buenos Aires again! But which stadium?
Here it is: Estadio Monumental, in Buenos Aires. The home of River Plate and Argentina's national team.
Allez! Which French stadium is this?
You got it, it's Stade Velodrome, in Marseille. The home of Olympique de Marseille.
A World Cup final was played here not long ago. Which stadium?
Spot on! It's Luzhniki Stadium, in Moscow. It hosted the 2018 World Cup final.
Last Hard question! Think about Africa. Which stadium is this?
The answer is FNB Stadium, in Johannesburg. Shaped like a calabash, it hosted the 2010 World Cup final.
Genius round! Only true football nerds will get these. Which stadium?
Yes! It's Estadio Centenario, in Montevideo. It hosted the very first World Cup final, in 1930.
Brand new and built for the biggest night. Which one is it?
That's Lusail Stadium, in Lusail. It hosted the 2022 World Cup final.
This one isn't just for football. Name it!
It's Beijing National Stadium, in Beijing. Nicknamed the Bird's Nest, it was built for the 2008 Olympics.
Painful memories for one big football nation. Which stadium is this?
Correct answer: Mineirao, in Belo Horizonte. Brazil lost 7-1 to Germany here in 2014.
Central Europe's newest giant. Which stadium?
Of course, it's Puskas Arena, in Budapest. Named after Ferenc Puskas, it opened in 2019.
Red and white on the outside. Which stadium is hiding here?
Boom! It's Stadion Narodowy, in Warsaw. It hosted the opening match of Euro 2012.
Derby day magic lives here. Which stadium is this?
Here it is: Stade Mohammed V, in Casablanca. Home to the famous Casablanca derby between Wydad and Raja.
Asia hosted the world here. Which stadium?
You got it, it's Seoul World Cup Stadium, in Seoul. It hosted the opening match of the 2002 World Cup.
A roof like a giant tent. Which one is it?
Spot on! It's Olympiastadion Munich, in Munich. Its tent-like roof was built for the 1972 Olympics.
Final question! One last Brazilian giant. Which stadium is this?
The answer is Morumbi, in Sao Paulo. The home of Sao Paulo FC.
Full time! That was a hard one. How many stadiums did you recognise? Drop your score in the comments, and subscribe for the next Quiz Rush!
